q: 1. The quantity of liquid waste which flows in sewers during rainy seasons is called
explain: Storm sewage (or storm water) refers to the runoff generated by rainfall during the rainy season.

q: 2. The self cleaning velocity, in order to prevent settling down of sewage in a large sewer is
explain: A velocity of approximately 0.75 m/s is required to ensure that solids do not settle at the bottom of the sewer pipes.

q: 3. The water carriage sewage system removes
explain: Water carriage systems use water as the medium to transport domestic, industrial, and often storm water through underground pipes.

q: 4. A separate system will be favourable when
options: the sewers are to be laid in rocks
the topography is flat necessitating deep excavation
explain: Separate systems are generally better for hilly terrain or rocky areas where storm water can be easily diverted into natural channels, or when budget for large combined pipes is limited.

q: 5. The internal diameter of the sewer should not be less than
explain: Standard engineering practice (and many codes) dictates a minimum diameter of 150mm (15cm) to prevent frequent clogging.

q: 6. For house drainage and lateral connection, we shall use
explain: Vitrified stone ware (clay) pipes are preferred for domestic drainage due to their resistance to corrosion and cost-effectiveness.

q: 7. Egg-shaped sewers are generally used for
explain: While best for combined systems to maintain velocity during low flow, they can technically be used in any system.

q: 8. For the sewers of diameter less than 600 mm, the type of joint preferred is
explain: Spigot and socket joints are standard for smaller diameter pipes, providing easy alignment and sealing.

q: 9. For the sewers of diameter more than 600 mm, the type of joint preferred is
explain: Collar joints are generally used for large diameter concrete pipes (over 600mm) for structural stability.

q: 10. A drop manhole is provided if
options: a sewer drops from a height
a branch sewer discharges into main sewer at a higher level
explain: A drop manhole is specifically used when the vertical difference between the branch sewer and the main sewer is more than 0.6m.

q: 11. In secondary treatment of sewage, the operation which takes place is
options: removal of heavier suspended inorganic material
removal of fine dissolved organic material
explain: Secondary treatment is biological; it uses microorganisms to decompose and remove dissolved and colloidal organic matter from the sewage.

q: 12. The equipment used for removing paper and rags from sewers is called
explain: A claw is a specialized tool used in sewer maintenance to snag and pull out rags, paper, or fibrous materials causing blockages.

q: 13. The amount of oxygen consumed by sewage from an oxidizing agent like potassium dichromate is
explain: COD measures the oxygen equivalent of the organic matter in a sample that is susceptible to oxidation by a strong chemical oxidant.

q: 14. B.O.D. represents
options: pollution strength of an organic fraction
pollution strength of bio-degradable organic fraction
explain: BOD measures the amount of oxygen required by bacteria to stabilize the *biodegradable* organic matter in water.

q: 15. In the B.O.D. equation K is called
explain: The constant 'k' (or 'K') represents the rate at which the organic matter is being oxidized (deoxygenation rate).

q: 16. B.O.D. test is not well suited to industrial wastes because
explain: Many industrial wastes contain toxic substances that kill the bacteria used in the test, making the BOD appear much lower than the actual pollution strength.

q: 17. Second phase B.O.D. is exerted because of the oxidation of ...........
options: carbonaceous matte into CO2 and H2O
explain: The first stage of BOD involves the oxidation of carbonaceous matter. The second stage, known as Nitrification or Nitrogenous BOD, occurs when specialized bacteria (Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter) oxidize ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates.

q: 18. Result of C.O.D. is generally higher than that of B.O.D. because ...........
options: the strong oxidising conditions in the test
complete oxidation of organic and inorganic compounds
the stables compounds are being oxidized
explain: The COD test uses a strong chemical oxidizing agent (potassium dichromate in acidic medium), which can oxidize nearly all organic compounds, including those that are biologically resistant (stable), leading to higher oxygen demand values.

q: 19. Presence of the following indicates recent pollution ...........
explain: Free ammonia or ammoniacal nitrogen is the first stage of nitrogen decomposition. Its presence indicates that the pollution occurred very recently and hasn't had time to oxidize into nitrites or nitrates.

q: 20. Partly separate system is ............
options: collecting D.W.F. and storm water in the same sewer
collecting D.W.F. and drainage of initial showers into the same sewer
collection of sewage and sullage into the same sewer
collection of storm water and a part of D.W.F. into the same sewer
explain: This system carries domestic sewage and the highly polluted 'first wash' of storm water in one pipe, while diverting clean excess rain to another.

q: 21. Leaping weir is provided only in ............
explain: A leaping weir is used in combined systems to allow dry weather flow to fall into an intercepting sewer while high-velocity storm water 'leaps' over it.

options: any waste water of domestic or industrial origin
explain: Sewage is the broad term for the liquid waste carried in sewers, originating from residential, commercial, and industrial activities.

q: 23. Sewerage is ............
options: collection + conveyance + treatment + ultimate disposal of sewage
explain: Sewerage is the complete science and infrastructure covering the entire path of waste from the point of origin to final disposal.

q: 24. A sanitary sewer is expected to run ............
explain: Sanitary sewers are usually designed to run half-full at maximum discharge to provide space for ventilation and prevent overflows.

q: 25. Time of concentration depends on ............
explain: Time of concentration (the time for water to travel from the farthest point to the outlet) is heavily influenced by the slope of the land.

q: 26. For a partly running circular sewer as the depth of flow increases ............
explain: As the depth of water in a pipe increases (up to a certain point), the cross-sectional area of flow increases, which increases the total discharge (Q).

q: 27. A fight sewer is provided when the gradient is ............
explain: In steep terrain, sewers must follow the slope while maintaining manageable velocities; specialized designs or 'flight' steps are used to manage the energy of the flow.

q: 28. When more than 2 sewers join in a manhole ............
options: their tops should be at the same level
their centres should be that the same level
their bottoms should be at the same level
explain: To maintain a smooth hydraulic profile and prevent backflow under pressure, the soffits (tops) of all incoming pipes should ideally be aligned with the soffit of the outgoing pipe.

q: 29. The working chamber of a manhole, along the direction of flow should have a minimum length of ............
explain: A minimum length of 1.2 m is required to provide enough space for a worker to enter, stand, and use tools comfortably for maintenance.

q: 30. 'Never discharge the contents of a bigger sewer into a smaller though the capacity of the later may be more due to steep slope' because ............
explain: Bigger sewers carry larger solids; if these enter a smaller pipe, they are much more likely to become lodged at the junction or in the pipe, causing a blockage.

q: 31. Before entering a manhole a candle is lowered into the manhole ............
options: to give a signal to the adjacent manhole
to find out presence of oxygen
explain: This is a traditional safety test; if the candle flame goes out, it indicates a lack of oxygen or a high concentration of non-combustible gases like CO2, making it unsafe to enter.

q: 32. A lamphole is helpful in ............
explain: A lamphole allows a light to be lowered into the sewer; by looking through the adjacent manhole, inspectors can check for obstructions or misalignments in the pipe.

q: 33. Colour of fresh sewage is ............
explain: Fresh sewage is typically a light grey or soapy color. As it becomes 'stale' or septic over time, it turns dark grey and eventually black.

q: 34. The factor deciding the length of a grit chamber is ............
explain: The length of the chamber is the product of the horizontal velocity and the required detention time for the smallest target particle to settle.

q: 35. Approximate percentage of the R.B.C. disc submerged under sewage is ............
explain: In a Rotating Biological Contactor (RBC), the discs are typically 40% submerged to allow the bacteria to alternate between feeding in the sewage and breathing in the air.
